\section[afirmar]{afirmar — to state, to assert}

\label{lesson:PT-C342-afirmar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for indisputable, then the Portuguese for to refute.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: afirmar}
\textbf{afirmar} — \textquotedblleft{}to state, to assert\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O jornal afirma que o preço do pão vai subir.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The newspaper states that the price of bread is going to rise.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Afirmar que} takes the indicative.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{afirmar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{affirmāre} \textquotedblleft{}to present as firm, to assert\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{ad} and \emph{firmāre} \textquotedblleft{}to make firm\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{firmus} \textquotedblleft{}firm\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{afirmar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{afirmar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{afirmar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for indisputable, then the Portuguese for to refute, then say \emph{afirmar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does afirmar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To state, to assert\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[a afirmação]{a afirmação — the statement, the assertion}

\label{lesson:PT-C342-afirmacao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to refute, then the Portuguese for to state.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a afirmação}
\textbf{a afirmação} — \textquotedblleft{}the statement, the assertion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Essa afirmação não é verdade.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{That statement is not true.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fazer uma afirmação} — to make a statement.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{afirmação} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{affirmātiō} \textquotedblleft{}affirmation, declaration\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{affirmāre} \textquotedblleft{}to assert\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{firmus} \textquotedblleft{}firm\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a afirmação}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a afirmação}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a afirmação}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to refute, then the Portuguese for to state, then say \emph{a afirmação} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a afirmação mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The statement, the assertion\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[fiável]{fiável — reliable, trustworthy}

\label{lesson:PT-C342-fiavel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to state, then the Portuguese for the statement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: fiável}
\textbf{fiável} — \textquotedblleft{}reliable, trustworthy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Este carro é velho, mas é muito fiável.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{This car is old, but it is very reliable.}
\end{quote}

European Portuguese; in Brazil \emph{confiável}. \emph{Uma fonte fiável} — a reliable source.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fiável} is built on \emph{fiar} \textquotedblleft{}to trust, to give credit\textquotedblright{} with \emph{-ável}; \emph{fiar} is inherited from Vulgar Latin \emph{fīdāre}, a form of Latin \emph{fīdere} \textquotedblleft{}to trust\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fiável}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fiável}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{fiável}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to state, then the Portuguese for the statement, then say \emph{fiável} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does fiável mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Reliable, trustworthy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[credível]{credível — credible, believable}

\label{lesson:PT-C342-credivel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the statement, then the Portuguese for reliable.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: credível}
\textbf{credível} — \textquotedblleft{}credible, believable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A história dele não é muito credível.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{His story is not very credible.}
\end{quote}

Of a person or a story. \emph{Pouco credível} — hard to believe.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{credível} is a learned formation on Latin \emph{crēdibilis} \textquotedblleft{}worthy of belief, credible\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{crēdere} \textquotedblleft{}to believe, to trust\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{credível}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{credível}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{credível}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the statement, then the Portuguese for reliable, then say \emph{credível} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[alegar]{alegar — to claim, to allege}

\label{lesson:PT-C342-alegar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for reliable, then the Portuguese for credible.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: alegar}
\textbf{alegar} — \textquotedblleft{}to claim, to allege\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ele alegou que estava doente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He claimed that he was ill.}
\end{quote}

Often of an excuse that may not be true.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{alegar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{allēgāre} \textquotedblleft{}to send with a commission, to bring forward, to cite\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{ad} and \emph{lēgāre} \textquotedblleft{}to send, to depute\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
